jiddaSpacedock.label: Jidda Spacedock
jiddaSpacedock.note: High above Jidda. Your ship is berthed at the end of the gantry. Walk to the teleporter at the far end and it beams you down to the crest pad.
jiddaSpacedock.intro: High above Jidda. Your ship is berthed at the end of the gantry. Walk to the teleporter at the far end and it beams you down to the crest pad.
jiddaSpacedock.name: Jidda Spacedock

npcs.name: Jest

lines.text: You keep your own boat?
Every ruler of Jidda has. You cannot govern water you have not been out on.
The lagoon is the road, the harbour is the market, and the tide does not care whose crest is on the pad.
What does Jidda need?
Hulls, hands, and somebody watching the Reach. Jamos keeps the first two on a board in the tavern. Job is the third.
And if you go west past the landing, go armed. That is not advice, it is the harbour rule.

npcs.bio: Rules Jidda from a room with no windows and a very long carpet. Learned the lagoon before learning the throne, and still keeps a boat at the crest dock.

npcs.name: Jamos

lines.text: You are the one to ask about crews?
I am the one to ask about anything that floats, and most things that do not.
Three boats went west to the Reach this season. Two came back. I have stopped writing the third one down and I have not stopped waiting for it.
What is out at the Reach?
Corsairs. And something they dug out of the sand that they should have left there.
Take Job if you go. Expect two refusals and then a fox already sitting in your boat.

npcs.bio: Keeps the harbour board out of the tavern — who is crewing, who is overdue, and who has stopped coming back. Knows every hull in the lagoon by its wake.

npcs.name: Job

lines.text: Three years running, they tell me.
Four. Nobody counts the first one because I was fourteen and the judges were embarrassed.
Jamos says you would come west with me.
Jamos says a great many things.
...Not wrong, though. That third boat had my cousin on it. Say when.

npcs.bio: Jidda’s champion on the break, three years running, and the only fox who will take a boat past the shoals in weather. Says the two are the same skill.

npcs.name: Jute

lines.text: You are the one off the transport. Good. Can you swing a mallet?
What is under there?
Gophers. Whole colony of them, and they have found the carrots.
Here is the thing nobody gets right the first time — do not wait for one to come up. By the time you see it, it has the carrot and it is already going back down.
So what do I hit?
The ground it is heading for. You can see them coming, if you watch the soil instead of the holes.
And mind the green ones. Those are my seedlings and they are coming up on their own. Hit one of those and you have done the gophers a favour.

npcs.bio: Works the only field on Jidda. Everything anybody on this planet eats that did not come out of the water came out of this one row, which is a thing he mentions.

npcs.name: Jago

lines.text: You have the look of somebody who has been west.
Corsair Reach.
Then you will have found the hollow on the Shoals and been told what you are missing.
I have read every corner of that map that has come through this room. I have never once been out there and I do not intend to start.
Why not?
Because I know what is sitting on top of that hole waiting for whoever does.

npcs.bio: Sits at the end of the tavern with his back to the room and a satchel he keeps a boot on. Has never been to the Reach and does not want to go.

npcs.name: Jetsam

lines.text: Everything on those shelves came out of the water. Some of it twice.
Anything worth having?
Depends where you are going. If it is west past the landing, take more than you think you need — nothing out there sells you anything.
And if I am going digging?
Then you want a spade and a corner of a chart, and I only stock one of those. Jago has the other, in the tavern, with a boot on it.

npcs.greeting: Everything in here came out of the water. Ask me what it was before.
npcs.bio: Buys what the lagoon gives back and sells it on to whoever needs it next. Has never once asked where a thing came from, which is why everything ends up here eventually.

npcs.name: Jarl

lines.text: Salt gets into everything. Leave a blade in the rack a season and the rack is holding rust.
The garrison keeps you busy?
The garrison keeps me honest. The boats keep me busy.
And if you are going out to the Reach — those corsairs carry flintlocks. Standing off at range to think about it is how you get shot. Close the distance, or do not go.

npcs.greeting: Say what you need. I will tell you whether the salt has had it.
npcs.bio: Keeps every blade on Jidda oiled against the sea air, a war he will tell you he is losing slowly. Has re-hilted the same sword four times for the same fox.

npcs.name: Jib

lines.text: Mind the rails. There is wax on everything in here and most of it is my thumbprint.
You shaped Job’s board?
I shaped four of them. He rides the ugliest one. Says it knows the reef.
Any advice for the heat?
Do not fight the wall. Stay in the pocket, drop in early, and if the lip comes over you, go with it — the barrel is worth more than anything you will ever do out on the shoulder.

npcs.bio: Shapes every board on the break, including the one Job has won on three years running — a fact he mentions about as often as Job does.

npcs.name: Jory

lines.text: Mind the ring. Stand in it long enough and somebody will take that as an invitation.
Eight bunks. How many are filled?
Six. The other two went west on the boat Jamos has stopped writing down.
So if you are going out to the Reach, go. Just come back and tell me what is down that hole, because I have to write something.

topics.label: Who taught you?
replies: The floor, mostly. Then a corporal off the west watch who is not here any more, and I would rather leave it there.
I wore that ring into the boards on my own, which is the only part of it I am proud of.

topics.label: What is the ring for?
replies: Anything that would otherwise happen in the mess. Grudges, bets, and cubs off the transport who need to find out what they do not know.
Twice a day, and everybody who lives here has been on their back in it, me included.

npcs.bio: Sergeant of the crest guard. Runs the ring in the floor twice a day and wore it there herself, one boot at a time.

npcs.name: Jem

lines.text: You are the one off the transport. You will be the talk of the mess by supper.
Anything moving out west?
Three sails. Every night, the same three. They do not come in and they do not go away.
Jory says that is not evidence. I say I have counted them for a month and she has counted them once.

npcs.bio: Just off the west watch and not yet out of her boots. Has counted the same three sails every night for a month and is waiting on a fourth.

npcs.name: Jed

lines.text: Mind your feet on that middle patch. It is hollow all the way under.
Hollow?
Runs. Gopher runs, right under the rows. Put a boot wrong and you are in one to the knee.
Jute has been at them all week with the mallet. He is losing, and he will not say so.
Stand on the plot and he will hand you one. He hands everybody one.

npcs.bio: Jute's hand. Digs the ditches, mends the fence, and has opinions about the east end of the plot that nobody asked for.

npcs.name: Jarrow

lines.text: HELP! The MOLES are eating all our crops, they recently became ANGRY and started multiplying. No one knows why.

topics.label: How do I play?
replies: Hit the hole it is HEADING for, not the one it came out of. By the time you can see a mole it already has the carrot.
Watch the soil between the holes — the ridge tells you which way it is going. And leave the green shoots be. Those are seedlings, and flattening one does the moles a favour.
Twenty carrots in the ground. Keep eighteen of them and you have done better than any of us have all week.

topics.label: The Machines are malfunctioning AND animals are becoming aggressive, why do you think?
replies: I think it’s because we FOXES have been abusing the power of our planets and cutting out crystals that are the planet’s heart.
We power our machines with the souls of our planets, and the creatures are from the planet. They are trying to tell us something.

npcs.bio: Works the seaward end of Jute’s field, which used to be the quiet end. Meets every boat that ties up at the farm now, because he has run out of other ideas.

npcs.name: Jody

lines.text: You have the look of someone who has never played this. Sit down, it is better that way.
What are we playing?
Four weights each, turn about. Only the side lying furthest up the board counts — and then it counts everything it has past the other fellow's best.
Which is why knocking mine off is worth as much as putting yours on. Most people work that out on the last weight. Usually mine.

topics.label: How do I take a shot?
replies: Put your finger on the weight, pull it back down the board, and let go. How far you pull is how hard it goes.
Past the first line or it comes straight off — that is the foul line and it is not a suggestion. Past the far rail and it is in the sawdust, unless it hangs over the edge, and a hanger is worth four.
There are no rails down the sides either. Half of what you learn here you learn out of the gutter.

topics.label: Four years at one table?
replies: Three, if you only count the ones I was sober for.
It is a good table. The wax is right and the light is over it, and nobody has ever asked me to move.

npcs.bio: Has not left the long board in four years and does not intend to. Wins on the last weight of the frame more often than anyone thinks is fair, and will explain why if you ask.

npcs.name: Julep

lines.text: Any chance you are looking for a job? We got great SMOOTHIES here, super fun to make.

topics.label: How do I make smoothies?
replies: Chop the fruit first — drag the knife down every red line, and keep the pieces even or it blends lumpy.
Then ice, then yogurt, both up to the band on the jug. Tip the chopped fruit in. Hold the button to blend and let go when the texture matches the ticket.
Then pour to the line and hand it over. Four customers, four orders. You will know if you got it right — they tell you.

topics.label: How did you get into the smoothie business?
replies: I was two seasons on a boat and I did not like any of it. Came back, sat on the crest with a bag of mangoes and a borrowed blender, and sold the lot before dark.
Built the deck myself the week after. The island would not have me — there is no flat ground on it — so I went out over the water instead.

npcs.bio: Runs the blender at the end of the crest deck. Has never once made the same smoothie twice and does not consider that a fault.

npcs.name: Jorn

lines.text: Busy morning?
The pad never stops and neither do I. Mind the mooring on your way past.

npcs.bio: Holds the crest mooring in a crest-painted skiff and asks every fox who comes off the pad what they are for. Has asked it nine hundred times and has never once been given an answer he liked.

npcs.name: Joss

lines.text: You run the heats?
I run the sheet. The water runs the heats.

npcs.bio: Keeps the heat sheet at the break — who is riding, in what order, and whether anybody should come looking for them. Has never entered and has watched more waves than every fox in the water put together.

npcs.name: Netter Pell

lines.text: Busy today?
Three nets and a torn seine, and the tide does not wait for any of it. Jetsam buys the cork off me when I cut it out.

npcs.bio: Mends nets on the item shop quay because the light is better there than at home. Has the only pair of hands on the lagoon Jamos will trust with a trawl.

npcs.name: Cooper Wray

lines.text: Anything I should know?
Do not buy a barrel off a boat. If it came in full it went out leaking, and I am the one who gets blamed for it.

npcs.bio: Coopers barrels for the item shop and for anybody shipping something that has to stay dry. Everything that leaves Jidda leaves in one of his.

npcs.name: Marram

lines.text: Good morning.
It is, actually. The grass took on the south bank at last — fourth year of trying. Give it a season and you will not see the sand move at all.

npcs.bio: Plants marram on the seaward banks so the islands stop walking into the lagoon a foot a year. Named for the grass, or it for her — she will not say which.

npcs.name: Brother Kelp

lines.text: Are you of the order?
I am. We are not only for the nave — somebody has to be standing on the quay when a boat is due and does not come.
Three names this season. Jamos keeps them on a board in the tavern. I keep them differently.

npcs.bio: Of the order, and sent down to the water. Blesses hulls before they go west and reads the names of the ones that do not come back, which is the part nobody thanks him for.

npcs.name: Bosun Tarn

lines.text: Waiting for something?
A crate. Due on the last ship, and the last ship came in light — which on this lagoon means it came in from west of where it should have.
Ask Jarl about it. He has re-hilted the same sword four times because my ferrules are in the same crate.

npcs.bio: Bosun off a hull that is currently in pieces on the armory slip. Waiting on a crate that was due on the last ship, and the last ship has been and gone.

npcs.name: Oarsman Dray

lines.text: You know everyone here.
By their walk, mostly. Faces change out here — a season of salt and sun and you would not know your own brother. Nobody changes how they cross a quay.

npcs.bio: Pulls an oar for anyone short a hand, and knows every fox on the lagoon by their walk before their face.

npcs.name: Sister Shoal

lines.text: You are a long way from the shrine.
Sent out to look at it. I had this place entirely wrong — I thought the water was what divided it. The water is the road.

npcs.bio: Novice of the order, newly of it, and still getting the early bells. Sent out to look at the harbour on the grounds that it is hard to pray for a place you have only seen from a window.

npcs.name: Fishwife Ivo

lines.text: Keeping well?
Between jobs. Have been a year. It suits me better than the jobs did, and the board sells out by noon either way.

npcs.bio: Sells whatever came up in the last hour off a board at the surf quay, and has been between proper jobs, cheerfully, for about a year.

lines.text: Welcome to Jidda, Steward.
Your ship is fuelled and berthed behind you. The teleporter at the end of the gantry puts you down on the crest pad in town.

topics.label: How do I get back to space?
replies: Walk back to your ship and board her. She will take you up to orbit.
